title: Distributed named entity recognition using parallel MapReduce and Stanford NER
abstract: Distributed named entity recognition using parallel MapReduce and Stanford NER occupies a distinctive place in the history of large-scale text analytics. The topic sits at the intersection of classical conditional-random-field sequence labeling, batch-oriented distributed computing, and contemporary demands for corpus-scale information extraction. This review examines recent journal literature relevant to that intersection, particularly the declining visibility of explicit Hadoop MapReduce implementations and the continuing analytical relevance of Stanford-style pipeline design. The review argues that the current literature contains few direct reimplementation of Stanford NER on MapReduce clusters; instead, the most relevant evidence comes from adjacent journal work on scalable biomedical, clinical, and domain-specific entity-extraction systems, which helps explain what aspects of the older architecture remain technically relevant and which have been displaced by Spark-native, toolkit-based, or transformer-based systems. Key themes include batch partitioning, model portability, inference locality, deployment economics, annotation normalization, and the tension between throughput and contextual richness. The review suggests that a major gap is the scarcity of direct peer-reviewed journal studies on Hadoop MapReduce and Stanford NER from 2020 onward. This scarcity is itself evidence of a field shift: away from explicit MapReduce orchestration and toward resource-centered toolchains and high-capacity neural inference.

title: Online Linear Programming for Multi-Objective Routing in LLM Serving
abstract: We study the online routing problem in large language model serving, where requests arrive sequentially and must be dispatched to parallel decode workers under tight batch-size and KV-cache constraints. Unlike widely used routing heuristics that are not tied to explicit service-level objectives (SLOs) and offer limited control over latency-throughput trade-offs, we introduce a multi-objective optimization framework that formulates routing as an online linear programming with interpretable decision rewards. We apply an efficient bid-price control policy based on the online linear programming that admits requests when their SLO-weighted benefit exceeds their shadow prices. To meet millisecond decision requirements, we develop a warm-started, projected first-order updates that track the evolving dual shadow prices online with predictable runtime. We integrate our router into the Vidur simulator and demonstrate substantial improvements over standard baselines across multiple SLO regimes, including end-to-end latency, time-to-first-token, throughput, and tail performance. A big picture from our result: a science-based approach outperforms others based on heuristics.

title: Research on Non-Balanced Data Over-Sampling Algorithm Based on Permuted Encoding SMOTE
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive and challenging issue in machine learning and data mining, where traditional classifiers frequently exhibit a strong bias toward the majority class, thereby neglecting valuable minority class information. To address this problem, the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) has been widely adopted; however, its reliance on linear interpolation within a single, fixed metric space often fails to capture complex nonlinear manifold structures, leading to over-generalization and boundary overlap. This paper proposes a novel over-sampling methodology named Permuted Encoding SMOTE (PE-SMOTE). By constructing multiple heterogeneous representation spaces through a sequence of random feature permutations and weight-encoding mechanisms, the proposed algorithm re-evaluates the topological neighborhood relationships of the minority class from diverse structural perspectives. During the variant generation phase, PE-SMOTE cross-references the nearest neighbors from distinct encoding spaces and incorporates a nonlinear modulation function to transform traditional one-dimensional linear interpolation into a multi-dimensional spatial generalization. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that PE-SMOTE effectively mitigates the risk of overfitting, reduces boundary ambiguity, and substantially enhances the diversity and quality of the synthesized samples, thereby establishing a smoother and more robust decision boundary for downstream classification tasks.

title: Beyond Classification: A Multilingual mBERT Framework for Sentiment Analysis, Zero-Shot Categorization, and Severity Assessment on social media
abstract: Considering the growth of multilingual user made content within social-media platforms, there is an urgent need for developing scalable, language-agnostic approaches for their analysis. Within this paper, we analyze mBERT's performance in sentiment classification in a binary setting as well as the possibility of performing transfer learning between languages. Specifically, the fine-tuned model is applied for sentiment analysis of tweets from the preprocessed TweetEval dataset, obtaining 79.2% of accuracy and 74.7% of the F1 score. It is shown that cross-language transfer learning without any preliminary training on multilingual sentiment datasets provides quite satisfactory performance. However, a more complex approach can be used, which consists of applying filtering of negative sentiments, categorization of subcategories through a sentence transformer with zero-shot settings, and grouping the resulting data in several major categories to obtain severity scores according to frequency thresholds. The application of the sentiment classification with transformers in combination with issue prioritization makes it possible to develop an end-to-end approach to structuring multilingual social media content.

title: From suspicion to violent action: A multi-category framework of fear speech using qualitative content analysis and machine learning
abstract: Current online hate speech flagging systems overlook more subtle forms of dangerous content that are not overtly violent, and more akin to what has been described as fear speech. Fear plays a crucial role in the process of radicalisation (Doosje et al., 2013), and is an important motivator of violence (Buyse, 2014). Yet, very little work has directly examined types and variations of online fear speech. In Study 1, we qualitatively content analysed a pre-annotated fear speech dataset to propose a novel framework of fear speech classification. This framework highlights a range of varying intensities of fear messages (Suspicion, Non-Violent Fear, Violent Fear, Non-Violent Call to Action, and Violent Call to Action). In Study 2, we generated synthetic data corresponding to our proposed framework, and used it to train a lightweight transformer-based model using contrastive learning, to enable automatic multilabel classification of fear speech. Our model outperformed multiple baselines, showing a decent ability to detect and classify fear speech. The proposed framework extends theorisation on hate speech and can be used to automatically detect less obvious harmful speech online, inform moderation policies and develop more appropriate counter fear-speech designs.

title: Unified counterfactual explainer for graph neural networks
abstract: Abstract Counterfactual explanations emerged as a powerful tool to unveil the opaque decision-making processes of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). However, existing techniques primarily focus on edge modifications, often overlooking the crucial role of node features and edge attributes changes in shaping the model predictions. To address this limitation, we propose a novel Unified Counterfactual Explainer (UCExplainer) for GNNs that generates counterfactual explanations for both node and graph classification tasks. Unlike prior methods, UCExplainer generates realistic and interpretable counterfactuals through a unified approach. It balances modifications by jointly optimizing perturbations across edges, edge attributes, and node features, ensuring the minimal changes required to flip a model’s prediction. Furthermore, UCExplainer offers maximum flexibility by supporting: (1) perturbations of both discrete and continuous values, (2) the clipping of values to a user-defined ranges, and (3) the exclusion of specific elements, such as entire nodes, edges, or individual features, from modification. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our approach over existing baselines.

title: An adaptive cost-sensitive machine learning framework for hospital length of stay prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of hospital length of stay (LoS) at admission is essential for bed management, staffing, and resource allocation. Administrative databases such as the French Programme de Médicalisation des Systèmes d’Information (PMSI) offer rich clinical information but exhibit strong heterogeneity across care units, making prediction challenging.We propose a cost-sensitive ensemble learning framework for LoS prediction in a multi-unit, imbalanced setting. The study includes 16,590 inpatient episodes across cardiology, general medicine, pediatrics, and neonatology, using only admission-level features. We evaluate Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), together with cost-sensitive variants of XGBoost based on inverse-frequency, square-root, and logarithmic weighting schemes, tested across α ∈ { 0.5,1,2 } . Performance is assessed using MAE, MAPE, R 2 , and extreme-LoS evaluation (LoS ≥ 8 days). XGBoost achieves the best global performance (MAE = 0.80 days, R 2 = 0.88 ). Cost-sensitive variants show comparable global accuracy (best MAE = 0.80); a small subset of configurations exhibit statistically significant but practically negligible differences in error distribution relative to the baseline (bootstrap confidence intervals overlapping; rank-biserial effect sizes ≤ 0.15 ). However, they systematically reshape the error distribution, producing selective improvements in rare long-stay cases depending on weighting formulation and intensity. In the extreme-LoS subgroup, models achieve MAE as low as 0.41 days and over 93% of predictions within a one-day error margin, with stable performance across configurations. Results also reveal substantial heterogeneity across clinical units, with better predictability in adult units than in pediatric and neonatal settings. Overall, boosting-based models provide strong and stable LoS predictions from administrative data, while cost-sensitive learning offers a mechanism to better capture clinically critical rare events without sacrificing global accuracy.

title: A Large-Scale Dataset and a New Method for RemoteSensing Traffic Object Segmentation
abstract: Remote sensing imagery plays a crucial role in evaluating regional transportation capacity. However, existing segmentation datasets often lack diversity in object categories and scenes, limiting the ability of models to comprehensively evaluate trans portation capacity in real-world scenes. To alleviate this gap, we construct a large-scale and diverse dataset for transportation object segmentation, named as NWPU-Traffic. This dataset encompass four traffic object categories (car, airplane, ship, and train) and a wide range of scenes from 49 cities across 7 countries, with instance-level annotations to ensure precise segmentation of individual objects, which bridges critical shortcomings in resolution and scene diversity in existing datasets. Leveraging this dataset, we establish a benchmark with several popular segmentation networks. Furthermore, we propose a novel segmentation method that leverages spatial-channel preserving feature interaction and an adaptive feature decoder, enabling robust segmentation across varying scales and complex environments. Extensive experiments and ablation studies validate the effectiveness of our approach. The dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/CVer-Yang/NWPU-Traffic.

title: Information Geometry Local Flattening SMOTE for Oversampling Imbalanced Data
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in modern data mining and machine learning, particularly in domains such as financial fraud detection, medical diagnosis, and network intrusion detection. Standard oversampling methods, notably the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), typically generate new samples via linear interpolation within a Euclidean space. However, real-world data often resides on low-dimensional nonlinear manifolds with distinct curvatures. By ignoring the intrinsic geometric structure of the data, Euclidean-based interpolation frequently generates synthetic samples that deviate from the true data manifold, leading to "boundary blurring" and "noise amplification." To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel synthetic oversampling method named Information Geometry Flattening SMOTE (IGF-SMOTE). The proposed framework treats the distribution of minority class samples as a statistical manifold and leverages the mathematical tools of Riemannian and information geometry. First, a localized non-parametric estimation approach is deployed to construct the local Fisher Information Matrix (FIM), which quantifies the informational curvature and metric of the data space. Second, a local flattening transformation matrix is derived from the eigenvalue decomposition of the FIM, projecting the curved local neighborhood into a flat isotropic Euclidean space where linear interpolation becomes statistically and geometrically valid. After synthesizing new minority samples within this flattened space, an inverse mapping is executed to project them back onto the original data manifold. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that IGF-SMOTE preserves the underlying probability density structure and successfully prevents "manifold detachment." Experimental evaluations across multiple public imbalanced datasets show that IGF-SMOTE consistently achieves superior performance in terms of G-mean, F1-score, and AUC compared to traditional SMOTE and its contemporary variants, offering a robust geometric perspective for learning from non-linear imbalanced data.

title: Research and Application of an Improved SMOTE Algorithm Based on Sparse Mask
abstract: In the fields of machine learning and data mining, the class imbalance problem is widely prevalent in practical scenarios such as credit fraud detection, medical diagnosis, and network intrusion detection. As a classic algorithm to address this issue, the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) synthesizes new samples by performing linear interpolation between minority class samples. However, the traditional SMOTE algorithm treats all features equally during the generation process, ignoring the correlation and heterogeneity of different features in the feature space. This easily leads to generated samples deviating from the true data distribution or even introducing excessive noise. To tackle this problem, this paper proposes an improved SMOTE algorithm based on a sparse mask, termed Sparse-mask SMOTE. By introducing a sparse mask mechanism, the algorithm dynamically and precisely controls "which features are allowed to generate changes." While maintaining the diversity of minority class samples, it strictly limits the random drift of core sensitive features and uncertain features. Theoretical analysis and logical derivation demonstrate that Sparse-mask SMOTE can effectively suppress manifold contamination and improve the quality of generated samples, thereby significantly enhancing the generalization performance of classification models on imbalanced datasets.

title: Research on Non-balanced Data Augmentation Algorithm Based on Encoding-Shift SMOTE
abstract: Class imbalance is a critical bottleneck that limits the generalization performance of machine learning models. Traditional Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and its variants typically synthesize new samples through linear interpolation within a single continuous float space. However, when applied to datasets that require switching among different encoding formats (such as float, integer, and quantized spaces), these methods often suffer from information loss, rounding errors, or distortion of the underlying data manifold. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling algorithm named Encoding-shift SMOTE. The core philosophy of the algorithm is to dynamically switch between different encoding spaces during the sample generation process. By designing projection operators among float, integer, and quantized spaces, we introduce a hybrid distance metric and an encoding-shift vector to guide the synthesis of minority class samples. This mechanism effectively captures the continuous geometric manifold while simultaneously incorporating the boundary characteristics of discrete and quantized spaces. Theoretical framework and algorithmic steps demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances the diversity and robustness of synthesized samples, providing an efficient and robust solution for class imbalance problems in complex data environments and resource-constrained edge computing scenarios.

title: Developing Digital Twins with SPADE for Autonomous Traffic Control
abstract: In this paper, we introduce SPADE, a framework engineered for building Digital Twins through Multi-Agent Systems. The architecture is inherently scalable and distributed, aligning perfectly with the demands of modern Digital Twin environments. We implement the Agents and Artifacts meta-model via the SPADE Artifacts extension, which serves as a structured interface connecting autonomous agents with their physical system counterparts. To demonstrate the framework’s efficacy, we detail a case study involving urban traffic management in Valencia, Spain. In this implementation, we model 386 street segments as individual agents responsible for managing traffic flows and coordinating redistribution efforts. The research delineates a MAS-based communication strategy spanning the entire network and introduces a consensus algorithm specifically designed to manage traffic rerouting when a street is closed. Finally, we present results from a series of experimental trials and evaluate the system’s broader potential. By synthesizing diverse data sources and providing an interactive dashboard for visualizing network conditions, this work demonstrates how SPADE can serve as a robust foundation for Digital Twin development, illustrating its potential for real-world urban applications through a conceptual implementation grounded in open sensor data.

title: Staging Is Necessary but Not Sufficient: Developmental Data-Attribution Laws, Transformers, and a Memorization Wall
abstract: Do the developmental data-attribution laws established in small hierarchical deep linear networks (parent study) -- an energy scaling law, a timing law, and a signed law -- transfer to a TRANSFORMER and to scale? Is the deciding variable the architecture, or whether the learner develops saddle-to-saddle -- and does that developmental setting even admit a clean attribution measurement? The deciding variable is NOT the architecture but whether the learner develops saddle-to-saddle -- and, crucially, whether that setting also admits clean attribution measurement. Using one gold-standard measure (leave-one-out retraining) applied identically across three testbeds: (1) STAGING GOVERNS TIMING -- a transformer that acquires its task holistically (in-context linear regression, one transition) has influence that is largest at initialization and decays (no developmental timing; energy scaling Spearman -0.17 vs shuffle -0.10), whereas the companion study's deep-linear network, which stages, has influence that peaks at its transitions. (2) A TRANSFORMER CAN GENUINELY STAGE -- in-context Markov next-token prediction makes a 2-layer transformer pass uniform -> in-context unigram -> in-context bigram, each a near-stationary saddle, converging to the Bayes-optimal in-context predictor; this staging is generic across 7/7 vocabulary, concentration, and architecture settings. (3) YET THE LAWS DO NOT ROBUSTLY TRANSFER even there, because gold-standard LOO needs a small fixed training set on which the staging transformer MEMORIZES (final loss far below the Bayes floor): across three seeds the influence timing is inconsistent (1-2/3) and the energy scaling matches a shuffle, and neither weight decay (to 0.6) nor enlarging the pool (M to 1024) suppresses the memorization. (4) THIS EXPOSES A MEASUREMENT WALL -- the conditions for clean developmental attribution (a small dataset with no memorization-generalization gap, which the deep-linear testbed uniquely has) and for saddle-to-saddle staging in a transformer (rich/streaming data) are in tension. A between-phase-mixture timing predictor transfers only weakly (Pearson 0.19) but still beats TracIn (0.07), static (0.00), and shuffle (0.04) baselines. We also document that a naively-scaled SGLD Bayesian influence manufactures an artifactual 0.43 'signal' that LOO refutes. Net: staging is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT to measure the laws in a transformer; the memorization wall -- not the laws being wrong -- is the central obstacle to developmental data attribution in transformers.This manuscript was generated autonomously by the AI Scientist running inside Claude Code (Anthropic); every reported number traces to the project's experiment outputs. title: An Observation-Model Inversion Based Oversampling Algorithm for Imbalanced Data: Observation-model SMOTE
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning and data mining, significantly undermining the classification performance of minority categories in real-world applications such as fraud detection, medical diagnosis, and anomaly detection. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and its variants address this issue by linearly interpolating between observed minority samples. However, these methods operate directly within the observed feature space and typically ignore the underlying data generation mechanism, rendering them vulnerable to generating noisy samples or exacerbating class overlap in the presence of observation distortions. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling framework named Observation-model SMOTE. Unlike traditional geometric interpolation, the proposed approach explicitly decomposes the data generation process into an "observation model inversion." We model the observed physical samples as the output of a deterministic nonlinear mapping from a pure latent state, corrupted by stochastic system noise. By employing first-order Taylor expansion and Bayesian inference, we mathematically invert this observation model to derive the posterior distribution of the latent states. Synthetic sampling is then performed within this noise-free, deblurred latent manifold, incorporating posterior uncertainty to enhance diversity. Finally, the newly synthesized latent states are mapped back to the feature space via the forward observation model to reconstruct realistic minority samples. Theoretical and qualitative analyses demonstrate that Observation-model SMOTE effectively isolates observation noise, preserves the intrinsic non-linear manifold topology, and adaptively regularizes decision boundaries, offering a rigorous and robust mathematical perspective for imbalanced manifold learning.

title: Uso de la inteligencia artificial para reducir los tiempos de producción en la gestión de eventos recreativos corporativos
abstract: Introduction. Corporate recreational event agencies often rely on manual routines that extend production cycles and increase rework. This study examines whether adopting generative AI is associated with reduced event production time. Methodology. A quasi-experimental before–after single-case design was conducted in a corporate recreational events company (Bogotá, Colombia) between June and September 2025. Three comparable events were produced under a traditional approach (no AI) and then with systematic ChatGPT support for creative and administrative tasks (concept development, proposal drafting, budgeting, and supplier selection). The dependent variable was total production time (hours) from brief reception to final approval. Given the small sample, the analysis prioritized paired differences, confidence intervals, and effect sizes. Results. A consistent reduction in total production time was observed across events (51 h, 60 h, and 69 h), yielding an average saving of 60 h (19.1%). The largest savings occurred in Concept Development (23.3 h) and Proposal Preparation (20.0 h), while Final Validation slightly increased (+1.3 h), reflecting additional quality checks. Conclusions. Findings suggest generative AI can be an efficiency lever for mid-sized agencies when combined with governance, training, and human verification. Results should be interpreted as applied and exploratory due to the small sample and single organizational setting. Future research should test replicability with more events and additional outcomes (cost, quality, and client satisfaction).

title: Comparative Study on the Ownership of Copyright of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Works
abstract: This article studies the question of copyright ownership for works produced by artificial intelligence. Taking China, the United States, and the European Union as the research subjects, a systematic analysis of the legislative provisions, administrative practices, and judicial precedents in each jurisdiction is conducted, concerning the copyrightability of AI-generated works and the question of rights attribution. On the basis of comparative analysis, this paper offers a theoretical review of the core disputes from the standpoints of the Lockean labour theory, the Hegelian personality theory, and the utilitarian theory. It constructs an analytical framework for distinguishing AI-assisted works from works generated autonomously by AI, with the substantiality of human participation as the core criterion, and puts forward a system of recommendations centered on a hierarchical ownership model. It advocates attributing copyright to the users of AI-assisted works that involve substantial human participation, establishing a special rights system with a shorter protection term for purely AI-generated works, and promoting the achievement of international coordinated consensus within the framework of the World Intellectual Property Organization, in keeping with the call of the Initiative for open, fair, and effective governance of artificial intelligence by all states.

title: GRASP: Graph-Reasoning Aided Survey Planning for High-Fidelity Related Work Generation
abstract: Writing a literature review requires a deep understanding of the relationships among cited papers: how they build on, challenge, or offer alternative perspectives to one another. We present Graph-Reasoning Aided Survey Planning (GRASP), a framework combining LLM planning for related work generation with graph algorithms to extract key relationships among cited papers. Our two-layer graph structure consists of a Graph of Thoughts and an Argument-Counterargument Planning Network, representing the cited papers at different levels of granularity, and we apply topology-aware pruning via a Steiner tree to identify the core inter-paper relationships captured in our graph. Our citation analysis-based evaluation shows that GRASP generates related work sections (RWS) that closely match human-written targets in terms of the discourse roles, intents, and grouping of citations.

title: Comparing Prompting Strategies and Backbone Choices for LLM Agents on Tabular Credit-Card Fraud Detection: An Empirical Study
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly proposed for financial decision tasks, yet their behaviour on tabular fraud detection has not been measured under a controlled protocol. This paper reports a head-to-head empirical comparison of four prompting strategies (zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, and ReAct-style tool use) across four LLM backbones (GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-Haiku, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct) on two public datasets: the ULB credit-card corpus with anonymised principal-component features and the Bank Account Fraud (BAF-Base) suite with human-readable attributes. All 32 agent configurations are benchmarked against logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM under identical temporal splits. Gradient-boosted trees retain a clear advantage: XGBoost reaches an AUC-PR of 0.847 on ULB and 0.196 on BAF, while the strongest agent configuration attains 0.412 and 0.153. The accuracy gap narrows substantially when features carry semantic meaning, and tool-augmented prompting yields its largest gain (+0.040 AUC-PR over chain-of-thought) on anonymised features. Inference cost remains three to four orders of magnitude higher for agents. A taxonomy of 400 manually coded errors indicates that agents most often miss fraud expressed through combinations of weak signals. Practical guidance for hybrid deployment is derived from these measurements.

title: DC-SMOTE: Dual-Consistency Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique for Imbalanced Data Enrichment
abstract: Class imbalance is a fundamental challenge in machine learning, often leading classifiers to bias toward the majority class and compromise the recognition of minority instances. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and its variants effectively enrich data diversity, their reliance on blind linear interpolation frequently disrupts the underlying geometric topology of the feature space. This oversight causes synthetic samples to encroach upon majority class regions, leading to over-generalization and severe class overlapping. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes Dual-consistency SMOTE (DC-SMOTE), a novel data augmentation framework governed by simultaneous input and output consistency constraints. Input consistency measures the topological similarity between synthetic instances and the original minority distribution via local density manifold alignment, ensuring statistical plausibility in the feature space. Concurrently, output consistency enforces symmetrical prediction constraints using a collaborative classifier, ensuring that the generated data adheres strictly to the existing decision boundaries without injecting ambiguous supervisory signals. By transforming the traditional random interpolation factor selection into a bounded joint optimization problem, DC-SMOTE dynamically calibrates the synthetic positions. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the algorithm effectively preserves the decision manifold and exhibits strong robustness across intricate non-convex data distributions, establishing a reliable foundation for imbalanced data learning.

title: Why the intellectual property of digital humans should be protected by copyright: insights from China’s legal system and case law
abstract: Abstract Digital humans have become a prominent new market phenomenon worldwide. However, applying intellectual property (IP) frameworks to this phenomenon remains in its nascent stage. This paper aims to explore effective pathways for protecting the IP rights of digital humans within the existing legal framework. Through textual analysis of Chinese legal texts and judicial cases, alongside references to EU, US, and Japanese precedents, this study argues that copyright protection offers the most rational and practical framework within China and may serve as a valuable reference globally. Centered on the core criterion of protecting human original creation, this paper systematically examines the applicability of copyright protection to the two key components of digital humans: appearance and driving mechanism. Regarding appearance protection, it contends that designs entirely created by humans may be recognized as works in the copyright sense, while program-generated appearances depend on the extent of human creative input. Additionally, the study addresses the resolution of conflicts between copyright and personality rights arising from appearances based on real individuals. Concerning driving mechanism, a distinction is drawn between human-driven and AI-driven processes. The paper proposes that the “Naka no Hito” (the person inside) aligns most closely with the legal status of performers, while AI-driven audio-visual outputs typically lack sufficient and identifiable human creative contribution to meet the originality threshold for direct classification as works. The findings indicate that integrating the original creation in the appearance and driving mechanism of digital humans into the existing copyright and neighboring rights frameworks can provide foundational protection. However, pressing challenges require further resolution, particularly in quantifying the originality threshold of human inputs—such as “prompts” in generative AI—and achieving systematic coordination of diverse rights across varying legal jurisdictions.

title: Carnap Ten Years Later: Lessons Learned and Next Steps
abstract: The first part of this paper provides an experience report, recounting the design and long-term maintenance of the Carnap proof assistant framework used cumulatively by over 45,000 students worldwide over the last decade. We cover the good, the bad, and the ugly: what worked well, what didn't work, and what added friction to development and maintenance over time. These insights motivate a bottom-up redesign of the Carnap framework, which is the topic of the paper's second part. Briefly, the new design combines a new high-performance verifier kernel (mm0-zig) targeting Mario Carneiro's metamath zero format, and the Aufbau Bytecode Compiler, (abc), a new proof compiler that can serve as a backend for richly interactive proof-authoring experiences on the web.

title: Optimizing Large Language Models for Causality Assessment in Pharmacovigilance: Developing a Performance Metric as Objective for Bayesian Hyperparameter Optimization
abstract: Background: Growing individual case safety report (ICSR) volumes have intensified demand for scalable automated causality assessment. Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise, yet performance on clinically demanding tasks remains suboptimal and inference-time hyperparameter optimization has not been investigated. Objective: To develop a Gaussian Process (GP)-compatible optimization objective and investigate whether temperature optimization improves LLM-expert agreement on Naranjo causality assessment of FAERS ICSRs. Methods: Expert causality assessments were performed on 723 stratified FAERS cases. OpenAI's GPT-5.2 was evaluated using chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting. Four composite metrics were developed: Weighted Cosine Similarity (WCS), Information-Weighted Agreement Score (IWAS), Entropy-Weighted Agreement and Cosine Similarity Score (EWACS), and Consensus-Weighted Cosine Similarity (CWCS) and Bayesian optimization using a GP surrogate with Probability of Improvement (PoI) acquisition was applied across temperature [0, 2]. Results: GPT-5.2 outperformed prior biomedical LLMs at baseline (T = 0), achieving 74.1% agreement on question 5 and 65.4% on question 10 of Naranjo algorithm. Entropy analysis identified these as the sole informative optimization targets. Temperature showed no systematic population-level effect (\b{eta} = 0.002, p = 0.959). EWACS-guided Bayesian optimization improved causality classification agreement from 45.0% to 72.0% (+27 pp), with the largest gain in Doubtful cases (+42.9 pp). Conclusion: EWACS was identified as the optimal GP-compatible metric. The absence of a universal temperature optimum indicates LLM performance is driven primarily by ICSR content, yet case-specific temperature selection produced meaningful improvements, supporting temperature optimization for LLM-assisted pharmacovigilance.

title: Design and Implementation of a Job Skill Entity Recognition (JSER) for Custom Entity Annotation using Trie Structure
abstract: Abstract—Named Entity Recognition in computer science is tricky because it uses terms and needs detailed annotations. Even though Named Entity Recognition has gotten better in uses it is not widely used in academic computer science. This paper presents JSER, a method that uses Natural Language Processing techniques to find and classify both known and unknown entities. Our approach uses Part-of-Speech tagging to pull out entities from unstructured text. We make annotations better and faster with techniques like tuning models adjusting thresholds and adding more data. JSER seems promising for tasks, like finding information analyzing text automatically and managing knowledge.

title: The Modulus-168 Cryptographic Seed: Breaking the Computational Bottleneck in Resource-Constrained PQC Networks
abstract: This paper introduces an optimized, resource-efficient asymmetric cryptographic primitives kernel based on the Learning With Errors (LWE) hardness assumption over bounded discrete lattices. While state-of-the-art post-quantum standards rely on large modulo operations (q > 2^12) that impose substantial computational overhead on resource-constrained embedded nodes, this framework introduces an engineered small-modulus quantization gauge fixed at q = 168. By scaling down the dimension topology (n = 4) and bounding the Gaussian noise distributions within an error bound vector, we demonstrate that an operational equilibrium can be achieved without inducing decryption failure or sacrificing security bounds. The proposed lattice-based construct successfully circumvents both polynomial-time quantum attacks (Shor's and Grover's factoring algorithms) and traditional basis reduction attacks (LLL and BKZ algorithms). Numerical simulations implemented in high-performance Python engines validate that the design achieves lower memory consumption and reduced pipeline overhead, rendering it optimal for low-power satellite communication networks and autonomous cyber-physical systems. Keywords: Post-Quantum Cryptography, Learning With Errors (LWE), Lattice-Based Cryptography, Small-Modulus Quantization, Resource-Constrained Embedded Systems.

Numerical simulations implemented in high-performance Python engines validate that the design achieves lower memory consumption and reduced pipeline overhead, rendering it optimal for low-power satellite communication networks and autonomous cyber-physical systems. title: Compatibility and Implication
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the logic of compatibility as a ground for the logic of conditionals. We identify a family of principles expressing key properties of compatibility, which can be coherently ordered. Assuming that conditionals are definable in terms of incompatibility—the negation of compatibility—each of the principles identified yields corresponding principles governing conditionals. Clarifying these derivability relations provides a new perspective on several existing accounts of conditionals.

title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Traffic Signal Control
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for adaptive traffic signal control. However, in safety-critical infrastructure like traffic control, the opaque, black-box nature of deep RL models poses challenges for transportation agency acceptance, regulatory compliance, operational trust, troubleshooting, and fine-tuning. To bridge this gap between high-performance optimization and human-comprehensible interpretability, this effort introduces a novel, explainable entity centric RL framework for safe and transparent traffic signal control. Rather than processing traffic states through monolithic, flat vectors, the proposed architecture disaggregates real-time intersection observations into distinct, high-dimensional lane entities and phase temporal configurations to inherently preserve the structural topology and geometric configurations of the intersection. Relational dependencies and inter-lane conflicts are dynamically extracted via a dual-stage attention network featuring sequential multi-head cross-attention and self-attention blocks. This design yields a real time affinity matrix that quantifies the direct influence of signal phases on specific approach volumes and queues, providing full visual and analytical interpretability. To ensure strict operational reliability, a deterministic action-masking interface is integrated directly into the Proximal Policy Optimization pipeline, explicitly blocking invalid phase transitions to guarantee absolute compliance with established signal timing and safety constraints. Evaluated in a microscopic simulation environment, outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in delay minimization. More importantly, the emergent attention weights align precisely with established traffic engineering principles, offering an auditable, trust-enabling, and deployable architecture for next-generation adaptive traffic control systems.

title: Supplementary data for "Can AI Help German Teachers Select Level-Appropriate Texts? A Cautious Framework for CEFR Estimation"
abstract: This dataset supports a small exploratory pilot that compared the CEFR-level estimates of three publicly accessible AI models (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5 Pro, and Llama 4 Scout) for 14 reading texts drawn from 7 German-as-a-foreign-language (DaF) coursebooks at levels A1, B1, and C1, published between 2021 and 2024 in Germany and Türkiye. Each text was queried once per model under identical zero-shot conditions using a single prompt (provided in English and German). Publisher CEFR labels are used as curricular reference points, not as independently validated gold standards.The package contains a codebook, a per-text coding table (anonymized metadata and each model's CEFR estimate, with agreement automatically computed against the publisher label), a summary of overall and by-level agreement, and the exact prompt and preprocessing conditions. Full coursebook passages are not included, as they are under copyright; the specific texts can be identified from the metadata and made available to editors and reviewers on request.

title: The Caller Is a Model: GPT-Realtime 2 as a Full-Duplex Synthetic Caller for Automated Voice-Agent Testing Infrastructure
abstract: User simulation for spoken dialogue systems has a two-decade history (Schatzmann et al., 2006), but classical simulators operate at the level of dialogue acts or text and cannot reproduce the acoustic, temporal, and full-duplex behavior that determines whether a deployed voice agent succeeds. We describe an implemented testing system in which a contemporary speech-to-speech model, OpenAI's general-availability Realtime model (the gpt-realtime alias, GPT-Realtime 2 family), serves as a high-fidelity synthetic caller that conducts live, real-audio calls into a hosted voice agent under test, driven by a reusable scenario and persona library, with each call captured, timed, and automatically asserted. Because the synthetic caller is itself a realtime model, it exercises behaviors that text-level harnesses cannot: barge-in and interruption, post-utterance silence, mid-utterance code-switching, and the turn-taking timing to which human callers are exquisitely sensitive (Stivers et al., 2009). We situate the approach within the user-simulation and machine-learning-systems-testing literatures and against the contemporary line of agent and full-duplex voice benchmarks -- tau-bench, tau2-bench, Full-Duplex-Bench, and the concurrent tau-Voice -- drawing the distinction that matters for deployment: those benchmarks evaluate which model to choose, whereas the system described here drives a live call into a deployed agent over its real telephony path to decide whether that particular agent is safe to ship, and serves as its regression gate. We describe the deployed components: the realtime caller, an audio bridge into the agent's call room, transcript and turn-timing capture, an assertion-based evaluator, and regression gating. The system is in production use as the continuous-integration verification gate for a multilingual voice agent, where it now serves in place of a manual user-acceptance cadence that previously required placing real phone calls by hand; whether it catches more production-relevant defects than that cadence is not yet measured. We report what the approach establishes, an honest limitation observed in use, namely that the realtime caller's own persona can drift, and an explicit statement of what the paper does not claim, and we identify multi-deployment measurement of defect catch-rate against the manual baseline as the remaining empirical step.

title: ALTCCO: an enhanced cuckoo catfish optimizer with LightTrack strategy for engineering design and UAV trajectory optimization
abstract: In this work, an enhanced metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed the Adaptive LightTrack Top-guided Cuckoo Catfish Optimizer (ALTCCO), is proposed to improve the performance of the original Cuckoo Catfish Optimizer (CCO) in solving complex numerical and real-world optimization problems. ALTCCO integrates three complementary strategies to reinforce population diversity, adaptive search, and convergence stability: (1) a bidirectional cross-interaction mechanism combining horizontal (dimension-wise) and vertical (segment-wise) crossover to enrich information exchange; (2) a LightTrack strategy incorporating historical position memory and stagnation-driven repulsive jumps to escape local optima; and (3) a top-guided adaptive mutation where mutation intensity is dynamically adjusted based on rank-based fitness to balance exploration and exploitation. ALTCCO was rigorously evaluated on 29 CEC2017 benchmark functions, five classic engineering design problems, and a high-dimensional 3D UAV path planning task in a complex constrained environment. Experimental results demonstrate that ALTCCO achieves superior convergence speed, optimization accuracy, and robustness across all test cases. On the CEC2017 benchmark suite, ALTCCO obtained the best results on 28 out of 29 benchmark functions and achieved the lowest average Friedman rank of 1.07 among thirteen competing algorithms. Additional high-dimensional experiments further confirmed its scalability, where ALTCCO maintained the best overall average ranks of 1.21 and 1.34 on the 50-dimensional and 100-dimensional CEC2017 benchmark sets, respectively. In the high-dimensional UAV path planning task, ALTCCO achieved the lowest mean path cost of 141.6121 with a standard deviation of only 2.2920, demonstrating excellent solution quality and stability. Statistical analyses based on the Friedman ranking and Wilcoxon signed-rank test further confirm the significant performance superiority of ALTCCO, establishing it as an efficient and versatile optimization framework for complex engineering applications.

title: GLOW-FDG: Generalized cancer LesiOn Whole-body segmentation model for $^{18}$F-FDG-PET/CT
abstract: Whole-body fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography combined with computed tomography is widely used in cancer care, but manual lesion delineation is slow, subjective, and difficult to scale. We present GLOW-FDG, an open-source artificial intelligence model for whole-body cancer lesion segmentation in fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography and computed tomography. The model was trained on 1,563 scans spanning multiple cancer types and evaluated on 185 external scans from independent institutions. Across breast cancer, nonmetastatic and oligometastatic lung cancer, head and neck cancer, and metastatic melanoma, GLOW-FDG consistently outperformed publicly available benchmark models in lesion detection, while reducing false positives and maintaining strong segmentation accuracy. Quantification of total tumor burden and total lesion glycolysis was robust across cohorts, and performance approached the variability observed between expert radiation oncologists. These results support GLOW-FDG as a generalizable tool for automated cancer segmentation and quantitative imaging biomarker extraction in whole-body imaging.

title: AI Systems: Statelessness Reinterpreted
abstract: This white paper defines the true causal architecture of modern AI systems and corrects the industry’s foundational misconceptions about statelessness, activations, and transitions. It formalizes the full mechanism chain—system prompt → interpretive state → runtime prior → state transitions → stability envelope—and demonstrates why reliability is an architectural property, not a behavioral one.

title: A Comparative Investigation of Cepstral Feature Extraction Methods for Deepfake Speech Detection
abstract: The widespread adoption of voice-based authentication systems has been accompanied by an escalating threat from deep learning-based synthetic speech generation techniques. This study presents a comparative and experimental investigation of cepstral feature extraction methods for deepfake speech detection. Specifically, Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), Linear-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (LFCC), and Constant-Q Cepstral Coefficients (CQCC) are systematically evaluated with respect to their frequency scaling characteristics, spectral resolution properties, and capacity to capture artifacts specific to synthetic speech production. Experiments were conducted on 5571 audio samples drawn from the ASVspoof 2021 Logical Access evaluation partition, with all methods assessed under identical classification conditions using a linear Support Vector Machine. Results indicate that CQCC attains the highest numerical performance, achieving 83.59% accuracy, 89.15% ROC-AUC, and 15.83% Equal Error Rate (EER); however, the performance difference between MFCC and CQCC does not reach statistical significance (p = 0.202). Five-fold cross-validation corroborates this finding (CQCC: 87.89% ± 0.81%). McNemar’s test confirms that the performance difference between LFCC and CQCC is statistically significant (p = 0.036). A fine-grained attack-wise analysis across 13 spoofing systems reveals that no single feature representation consistently outperforms the others across all attack types; CQCC achieves the highest accuracy on 6 out of 13 systems, while MFCC remains competitive on several attack categories. The overall findings indicate that deepfake detection performance is highly sensitive not only to the classifier architecture but also to the choice of frequency scale, cepstral transformation design, and data conditions. Empirical motivation is provided that multi-feature strategies integrating complementary frequency representations may offer more robust and generalizable detection solutions.

title: DBCore: Shaping generalizable decision boundaries for coreset selection
abstract: Coreset selection for classification often relies on assessing individual sample difficulty or importance, leading to sample-wise or range-based selection, but this can overlook the collective impact on model decision boundaries. Realizing that the representative power a coreset possesses is tightly associated with the decision boundaries a model can form on it, we propose a novel approach that directly optimizes the Decision Boundary (DB) formed by the selected coreset. Specifically, we ask: How can we collectively select samples to create a DB that is globally smoothed yet locally detailed, ensuring maximum generalizability and noise-resilience to the original dataset? To address this, we define two key objectives: (1) Global shape retention – The selected coreset should form a smoothed version of the original DB, preserving its overall structure and preventing overfitting; (2) Local detail preservation – While smoothing prevents overfitting, excessive smoothing risks losing critical nuances. Thus, the selection must also retain key points near the original DB to capture local complexities. We formulate these objectives as a convex quadratic optimization problem with linear constraints and solve it efficiently. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the consistent and substantial advantages of our method over the state-of-the-art coreset selection strategies. The source code is available at https://github.com/diqichen91/DBCore.git .

title: SABLE: An NDA-Safe Closed-Loop LLM Framework for Analog Circuit Optimization in Industrial EDA Flows
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can propose circuit-optimization decisions, but industrial analog flows cannot expose foundry PDK content, proprietary schematics, absolute simulation paths, or license-bound tool state to a cloud endpoint. We present SABLE (Safe Analog Boundary for LLM-driven EDA), an NDA-safe closed-loop framework that lets LLMs optimize analog circuits through Cadence Virtuoso, Maestro, and Spectre while returning only scrubbed topology intent, numeric metrics, operating-point summaries, and scoped writeback status. "NDA-safe" denotes enforcement under a stated curious-but-passive cloud-provider threat model, not a formal non-interference proof. The framework combines an explicit threat model, a whitelist of 28 scoped SKILL entry points, PDK/path/model scrubbing on every return path, structured Maestro setup and writeback, a strict JSON action contract with six machine-checked stop conditions, and best-so-far state preservation. We evaluate eleven LLM checkpoints from the same documented reset state on two real closed-loop tasks, both run as process-voltage-temperature (PVT) sign-offs across three corners: a 20 GHz LC-VCO tuning-curve task and a two-stage op-amp task. On the LC-VCO task 7 of 11 models pass; on the harder op-amp task, where every metric must hold at the worst corner and a phase-margin gate rejects unstable high-gain points, 4 of 11 pass within a 15-iteration budget. Feedback-path ablations show that removing individual sanitized channels either silently weakens the specification or degrades the search. Model quality differs sharply once the loop requires tool discipline, bias reasoning, and specification repair, yet an NDA-safe boundary still provides enough sanitized feedback for successful analog circuit optimization.

title: Latency Is the Product: The Systems Envelope as the Binding Constraint in Production Realtime Voice Agents
abstract: Public discourse and academic benchmarking around conversational AI center on model capability: reasoning, comprehension, and accuracy on held-out tasks. Yet in production deployments of realtime voice agents, the determinants of success lie largely below the model layer. Drawing on the deployment of a multilingual realtime voice receptionist for a multi-office field-services business, together with published findings on human turn-taking and machine-learning systems engineering, this paper argues that the binding constraint on a deployed conversational agent is its systems envelope: the end-to-end latency budget, telephony and back-office integration, conversational context and state management, the handling of disclosure and caller trust, and, most neglected of all, organizational adoption. Human conversation tolerates a gap between turns of roughly 200 ms (Stivers et al., 2009), a budget that contemporary cascaded and even end-to-end speech architectures struggle to honor once retrieval, tool use, and call routing are introduced. We propose task resolution without human handoff as the primary evaluation metric for deployed agents, in contrast to comprehension- or accuracy-based proxies measured on demonstration-path distributions that do not resemble production traffic. We offer a field taxonomy of production failure modes, an explicit statement of evidentiary scope, and an explicit statement of what the paper does not claim. The contribution is a reframing for both practitioners and researchers: optimize the envelope, not only the model.

title: Coupling Information Space Dynamics with LLM-Free Semantic Graph Retrieval: A Kinematic Control Layer for Graph-Based RAG
abstract: LiteSemRAG [1] demonstrates that a heterogeneous semantic graph, built entirely fromcontextual token-level embeddings, can match or exceed the retrieval quality of LLM-drivengraph-RAG systems while consuming zero generation tokens. Its indexing and query-time mechanisms,however, are governed by static thresholds and state-blind edge weights: they do notcondition on the trajectory of the conversation that produced the query. Information SpaceDynamics (ISD) [2] models an LLM’s behavioral state as a trajectory on a differentiable manifoldand supplies three kinematic observables — reference drift δ(t), geodesic turning curvatureκ(t), and torsional resistance τ (t) — that quantify exactly the kind of trajectory informationLiteSemRAG’s static design discards. This paper develops a formal coupling between the twoframeworks. We show that LiteSemRAG’s index space is a subspace of ISD’s ambient Hilbertspace H; we replace LiteSemRAG’s fixed anomaly threshold with a drift-integrated threshold; wereplace its static co-occurrence edge weight with a curvature-dampened weight; and we replaceits absence of an escape mechanism with the ISD shock operator, routed through LiteSemRAG’sown isolated semantic recovery channel. Each coupling is presented as a testable empirical hypothesis,consistent with ISD’s Principle of Pure Observability, and each equation is checked fordimensional and structural consistency against the source formalisms of both papers.

title: Dimensional Folding SMOTE: Over-sampling High-Dimensional Imbalanced Data via Structural Patch Recombination
abstract: High-dimensional imbalanced data classification poses a significant challenge in machine learning and data mining, where the joint impact of the "curse of dimensionality" and "class imbalance" heavily degrades the performance of traditional classifiers. Standard over-sampling techniques, such as SMOTE and its variants, often fail in high-dimensional spaces due to distance concentration, which invalidates nearest-neighbor metrics and leads to the generation of out-of-distribution noise or severe class overlapping. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel and efficient over-sampling algorithm named Dimensional Folding Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (DF-SMOTE). Instead of relying on traditional global dimensionality reduction techniques that risk losing crucial non-linear manifold information, the proposed algorithm introduces a "dimensional folding" mechanism. This mechanism systematically maps the sparse, high-dimensional feature space into multiple compact, low-dimensional "structural patches" with predefined overlap. By projecting the features into lower-dimensional sub-spaces, the discernibility of Euclidean distance is effectively restored, enabling the accurate construction of local topological neighborhood graphs for the minority class. Within each individual patch space, an independent interpolation and a cross-sample "structural patch recombination" strategy are executed. This strategy breaks the rigid linear constraints of conventional high-dimensional interpolation and synthesizes new patch components that strictly adhere to the underlying local manifold. Finally, an "inverse folding expansion" operator smoothly reassembles and expands these synthesized low-dimensional patches back into the original high-dimensional space through a weighted fusion mechanism for overlapping features. Theoretical analysis indicates that DF-SMOTE effectively mitigates the distance concentration problem, significantly enriches the spatial diversity of the minority class without injecting noise, and maintains a linear time complexity relative to the feature dimension. Consequently, the algorithm provides a robust, scalable, and geometrically sound data-level solution for empowering standard classifiers to handle ultra-high-dimensional imbalanced learning tasks.

title: Boosting the Transferability of Adversarial Attacks with Semantic-Invariance and Low-Gradient Replacement
abstract: Deepneural networks are highly vulnerable to adversarial examples, which are generated by introducing subtle perturbations to input data to mislead model classification. Currently, transfer-based attacks are prevalent in adversarial example generation and can be categorized into input transformation-based and gradient-based methods. However, most input transformation-based methods tend to produce augmented replicas that are semantically inconsistent with the original inputs, while gradient-based methods often leave low-gradient regions unperturbed within the model’s critical attention areas. These limitations constrain further improvements in adversarial transferability. In this work, we propose a Semantic-Invariance and Low-Gradient Replacement Method (SLRM) to address these challenges. Our framework integrates semantically consistent augmentation and gradient replacement as follows: (1) a feature extractor captures semantic features from original inputs and a reconstructor generates augmented replicas that preserve semantic fidelity to enhance input diversity, and (2) low-gradient regions in adversarial examples are systematically replaced with corresponding regions from augmented replicas to eliminate the under-perturbed areas critical for model robustness. Comprehensive empirical evaluations on ImageNet demonstrate that SLRM significantly enhances the transferability of baseline methods and seamlessly integrates with state-of-the-art approaches to further improve their performance. Moreover, SLRM substantially improves the robustness of baseline methods against defended models, achieving superior attack success rates under advanced adversarial defenses.

title: The Irreducible Agent: A Dual-Layer Architecture for Coherent Long-Horizon Intelligence
abstract: O Agente Irredutível propõe uma arquitetura de dupla camada para inteligência artificial de longo prazo, operando em ambientes onde trajetórias futuras completas não podem ser comprimidas com segurança em um único plano inicial. A estrutura é motivada pelas consequências operacionais da irredutibilidade computacional, evitando explicitamente a afirmação de que as trajetórias dos agentes são universalmente ou formalmente irredutíveis. Em vez disso, a irredutibilidade é tratada como uma restrição arquitetônica: em muitas tarefas do mundo real, informações relevantes, dependências, compromissos e condições ambientais emergem apenas durante a execução. A arquitetura introduz duas camadas complementares: λ-PDCA, uma camada de continuidade de execução que organiza a agência de longo prazo como ciclos interligados de planejamento, execução, observação, verificação, adaptação, transferência de estado e continuação; Δ-Coerência, uma camada de verificação de continuidade projetada para avaliar se um agente preserva objetivos, compromissos, restrições, dependências de memória, valores e obrigações relacionais enquanto adapta suas estratégias locais. As duas camadas são acopladas por meio de uma função de governança, Γ(ΔC_t,C_t,V_t), que mapeia evidências de coerência em modos de execução como continuar, inspecionar, replanejar, reduzir a autoridade, escalar ou parar. Isso produz uma arquitetura de circuito fechado na qual a continuidade não é meramente medida após a ação, mas se torna causalmente relevante para a próxima transição admissível do agente. O artigo distingue entre continuidade de objetivos, continuidade de planos e continuidade de trajetórias; introduz o conceito de memória de continuidade; identifica modos de falha característicos, como desvio de objetivos, perda de comprometimento, conclusão falsa, colapso de verificação e estagnação aparentemente coerente; e propõe um programa experimental falseável com cinco hipóteses e uma família de benchmarks controlada com base em Trajetórias com Comprometimento. A tese central é que a inteligência de longo prazo não deve ser entendida como previsão estendida indefinidamente. Em vez disso, deve ser entendida como a capacidade de continuidade coerente sob condições em evolução. O princípio arquitetônico proposto é: Agente Irredutível = Execução Adaptativa + Continuidade Verificada + Transição Governada, e sua formulação conceitual mais ampla é: Inteligência é a arte da continuação coerente.

title: REAP: Reproducible Embeddings via Averaged Projection
abstract: REAP (Reproducible Embeddings via Average Projection) - first tagged release, archived on Zenodo for citation. REAP builds a stable consensus topic space from multiple UMAP runs by averaging distance matrices rather than coordinates. Then places new, unseen data / documents into that space with a trained projection head. This is a pre-v1 release. The API is usable and tested.

title: UHA: UltraCore HyperAlgebra — A Formally Verified n-Dimensional Algebraic Carrier over ZMod(2^64) in Lean 4
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of UHA, an n-dimensional algebraic carrier over the finite ring ZMod(2^64), targeting branchless 64-bit hardware arithmetic. Verified layers include pointwise addition and scalar multiplication (yielding a U64-module structure) and a class of norm-preserving operators (UOp), whose unitary-like property is proved as a first-class obligation on every instance. General multiplication (mulWith) is left as an explicit open specification: its structure-constant tensor and concrete algebraic realization are deferred to external branchless C++/CUDA kernels, following the project's principle of honest separation between verified scaffolding and unverified numerical content. Part of the UltraCore/ComplexBit series. Released under Apache License 2.0 (code) / CC BY 4.0 (paper).

title: Measuring the Dialect Ladder: When Structured Inter-Agent Messages Pay Off, and When Comprehension Breaks
abstract: A companion empirical study to SynAP (doi:10.5281/zenodo.21176725). We measure the two lowest rungs of SynAP's dialect ladder against real hosted models (Ollama Cloud), holding payload content constant while varying representation and size. Three findings: (1) the typed dialect's token cost crosses below natural language at ~5 structured records; (2) representation changes cost but not comprehension (identical across all conditions), so efficiency and fidelity are separable axes; (3) comprehension degrades with payload size and is driven by the model, not the dialect (one model holds 100% where two collapse) - the regime the protocol's proof-of-understanding acknowledgment exists for, where the remedy is a different receiver rather than a dialect downgrade. Harness and exact numbers released for reproduction.

title: INTELLIGENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM FOR DIGITAL MARKETING COMMUNICATIONS BASED ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND CHATBOTS
abstract: Topicality. The article substantiates a conceptual approach to optimizing and ensuring cybersecurity of digital communications management systems of enterprises by forming a single integrated information space of a business entity. The relevance of the study is due to the rapid deployment of artificial intelligence (AI), which has led to the emergence of specific cyber threats and risks of compromising confidential information at the points of infrastructure integration of linear MarTech platforms. The subject of the research is methods, models and tools for building an intelligent digital marketing communications management system based on artificial intelligence technologies, as well as mechanisms for ensuring its cybersecurity, verifying protection circuits and assessing the effectiveness of functioning in the context of the integration of digital MarTech platforms. The purpose of the article is to develop a conceptual model of an intelligent digital communications management system with verification of its security contours and the formation of an applied mathematical apparatus for assessing its effectiveness. The following results were obtained. A four-circuit architecture of the digital communications management system has been formed, where the basic digital infrastructure circuit acts as a source of primary data for the analytical AI core, and the security of access to CRM systems is regulated by a separate feedback loop. The information flows of the system have been formalized based on a set-theoretic approach using input parameters (set X) and output control signals (set Y), which record text and voice information protocols of dialogues. A model of integral evaluation of the system has been proposed, which consolidates operational-information, security and performance parameters. The results of calculating the eigenvector of the matrix using the T. Saati MAI (under the condition of full consistency, where VU = 0.69% < 10%) allowed us to determine the objective weighting factors of the system. It was found that the cybersecurity coefficient (γ = 0.297) and the level of automation of circuits (α = 0.163), which function in synergy with the productivity index (β = 0.540), are of great importance for ensuring the reliability of the architecture. Conclusion. The significance of the work lies in determining the strategic prospects for data protection through the deployment of a zero-trust architecture and AI governance standards, which protect personal data from unauthorized fine-tuning of public neural networks during operation.

title: IPDiff: Diffusion-driven ORSI Salient Object Detection with Information Reconstruction and Multi-Prior Guidance
abstract: Existing Salient Object Detection in Optical Remote Sensing Image (ORSI-SOD) methods mainly adopt the static inference strategy, which uses fixed trained model parameters for saliency inference in the testing phase. This means that even if the generated saliency map has errors, it cannot be further optimized. In this paper, we propose the novel IPDiff, a Diffusion-driven ORSI-SOD method with Information Reconstruction and Multi-Prior Guidance. We build IPDiff based on a unique dynamic optimization strategy, which endows IPDiff with the ability to iteratively optimize saliency maps with a dynamic parameter. Specifically, we formulate ORSI-SOD as a conditional diffusion problem in IPDiff. IPDiff first extracts informative conditional priors from ORSIs, including the saliency prior and the hierarchical priors, in the prior network with the assistance of the information reconstruction-driven attention module. The saliency prior can provide positional information of salient objects, while the hierarchical priors can provide specific detail and semantic information of salient objects. Under the guidance of these priors, IPDiff then iteratively denoises random noise as the timestep dynamically changes in the denoising network, generating saliency maps that are close to ground truths. Notably, we simultaneously supervise IPDiff in both spatial and spectral domains through a hybrid loss function to achieve efficient network training. Comprehensive experiments on public ORSSD, EORSSD, and ORSI-4199 datasets demonstrate that our proposed IPDiff achieves the best performance compared to 46 state-of-the-art methods. The code and results of our method are available at https://github.com/MathLee/IPDiff.

IPDiff first extracts informative conditional priors from ORSIs, including the saliency prior and the hierarchical priors, in the prior network with the assistance of the information reconstruction-driven attention module. The saliency prior can provide positional information of salient objects, while the hierarchical priors can provide specific detail and semantic information of salient objects. Under the guidance of these priors, IPDiff then iteratively denoises random noise as the timestep dynamically changes in the denoising network, generating saliency maps that are close to ground truths. Notably, we simultaneously supervise IPDiff in both spatial and spectral domains through a hybrid loss function to achieve efficient network training. Comprehensive experiments on public ORSSD, EORSSD, and ORSI-4199 datasets demonstrate that our proposed IPDiff achieves the best performance compared to 46 state-of-the-art methods. The code and results of our method are available at https://github.com/MathLee/IPDiff.

title: Mathematics Behind Enigma and Its Breaking
abstract: This paper explores the applications of mathematics in cryptography through the study of the Enigma machine and its cryptanalysis. During World War II the German armed forces used the Enigma machine for highly encrypted communications. The Allied forces initially faced significant challenges in breaking its encryption. This study analyzes the mechanics of the machine and the mathematics behind it. The study further analyzes the mathematical logic employed by Marian Rejewski and Alan Turing to decode it. The study highlights how mathematical reasoning and pattern analysis enabled the reduction of vast possible configurations, ultimately helping in successful decryption. The mathematical ideas used to break Enigma remain relevant in protecting digital communication today.

title: PHILIA OS Phase 2 — Input Scaling Layer Validation: Pre-Registration (94th DOI)
abstract: This document constitutes the pre-registration for the 94th DOI of the PHILIA OS research series (Trinity AI Research Team, Konyang University). title: An Index-space SMOTE Algorithm for Imbalanced Data Augmentation
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning and data mining, where standard classifiers often exhibit a bias towards the majority class, leading to severe misclassification of rare but critical minority instances. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and its variants have been widely adopted to alleviate this issue via linear interpolation, they predominantly operate within continuous feature value spaces. Consequently, these methods often fail to capture the underlying structural relationships or arrangement regularities embedded within feature index patterns, particularly in high-dimensional or structured data domains. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a novel data augmentation framework named Index-space SMOTE. Unlike traditional approaches, the proposed algorithm shifts the analytical paradigm from the conventional feature-value space to a topological feature index space. By mapping minority instances into distinct feature index sequences, we define a set-theoretic distance metric based on Jaccard similarity to accurately identify nearest neighbors within the structural domain. Synthetic instances are then generated using a probabilistic combination mechanism applied to the intersection and union of the parent index sets, thereby synthesizing completely new structural configurations while preserving the core, shared feature skeletons. Finally, the corresponding feature values are reconstructed through localized interpolation restricted to the active index boundaries. This method effectively prevents overfitting and suppresses the generation of boundary noise. The index-space formulation provides a fresh and robust perspective for handling complex, structured, and high-dimensional imbalanced datasets.

title: A Bit-Level SMOTE Algorithm for Binary Feature Oversampling
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, commonly encountered in applications such as fraud detection, medical diagnosis, and network intrusion detection. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is a well-established solution, it and most of its variants operate within continuous feature spaces. When applied to datasets with binary encodings—such as high-dimensional bag-of-words models, multi-label vectors, or hashed representations—traditional SMOTE generates continuous real numbers. Subsequent binarization via thresholding often compromises the intrinsic topological structure of the data and introduces unwanted noise. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an innovative Bit-level SMOTE algorithm. Diverging from traditional paradigms that perform linear interpolation at the continuous feature layer, the proposed method operates directly at the binary representation layer to achieve structural combination and crossover generation. Bit-level SMOTE employs Hamming distance to establish an accurate proximity metric in discrete spaces. By utilizing logical bitwise operators (such as XOR and XNOR), the algorithm systematically decomposes the features of a base sample and its nearest neighbors into consistent regions and differential regions. Consistent features are strictly preserved to maintain the underlying structural dependencies, while differential features are adaptively recombined using a controlled probabilistic framework. Theoretical analysis indicates that Bit-level SMOTE effectively synthesizes high-quality binary minority samples that conform strictly to the original discrete manifolds. Furthermore, by retaining structural sparsity, the algorithm avoids inflating matrix density, ensuring computational efficiency and hardware-friendly execution through fast bitwise operations. This research provides a robust and mathematically coherent framework for oversampling in pure binary feature domains.

title: NeuroOnline: Bridging Pretraining and Online Adaptation for EEG Foundation Models
abstract: EEG foundation models have shown strong potential in learning generalized representations across subjects and tasks. However, most existing approaches follow a pretraining-static deployment paradigm, which suffers from two key limitations: (1) misalignment between pretraining objectives and downstream tasks, and (2) limited adaptability to distribution shifts in online settings. We propose Online Neural Adaptation (NeuroOnline), a unified framework that enables continuous adaptation in online scenarios. NeuroOnline integrates two complementary mechanisms: (1) multi-view consistency learning, which enforces cross-view alignment to promote consistent and task-relevant representations, and (2) context-aware representation modulation, which leverages a learnable context prompt with cross-attention to dynamically adapt representations to evolving data distributions. Together, these mechanisms unify representation alignment and dynamic adaptation. Experiments on multiple EEG benchmarks show that NeuroOnline consistently outperforms strong baselines in online settings, achieving better performance under distribution shifts. Ablation and sensitivity studies further validate the necessity of each component and the effectiveness of the overall design.
